parent.digest: the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the issue's body field as the GitHub REST API returns it

safety.meaning: unique authority, checked bytes, acknowledged coverage before successor service, replay at the logical cut and deposition ending emission

containment.meaning: the fault stays inside its class: refusals change nothing, host loss keeps the volume and generation, and damage is accounted by physical unit

retention.meaning: every member of S at the certified cut and frontier that stays eligible is served its exact bytes, or lies on an accounted damaged unit

progress.meaning: recovery reaches Live and serves within its bounds, with H under R6 and F declared apart

conservation.meaning: at the publish-aligned boundary transient residuals are zero, units have one owner and protected history is counted, not reused

cycles.evidence: seeded sampled cycle histories of the production takeover history world: counts, work and ticks, never hardware latency; seeds 1 to 16 at 32 cycles are unpowered discovery

components.evidence: composed projections of two accepted protocol models at each cross-model interface, checked exhaustively from their declared prefixes within their declared bounds: no inductive proof and no implementation refinement

histories.evidence: implementation history evidence: the production owner, storage, routing and client path recorded as histories the oracle judges for positive preservation, credited by outcome with no model-to-Rust trace replay

proxies.evidence: the packages' simulated-device proxies: same-host warm recovery over the simulated device, uncredited for hardware

packages.evidence: observed class-bound hardware packages, judged from lane receipts and raw artifacts by scripts/recovery-packages.py

volume-loss.evidence: the reconciler's actual-volume-loss decision and cold provisioning, apart from every host-loss path

comparisons.evidence: calibrated comparison receipts under the frozen frame, statistics and policy, judged by scripts/measurement-frame.py report with H by scripts/hit-gate.py

host-loss.meaning: host loss with warm takeover: the recorded standby, or a designated fresh host after owner and standby loss, takes over the surviving volume at its volume identity and generation and restores S from the certified cut

unrun.store: the store column is conditional: #123 records no ST1 to ST8 qualification, and no store observation is a cited receipt

same-host-restart.meaning: the owner restarts on its own host and volume and restores S from the certified cut

unrun.model: no model projection runs a same-host restart; the joins project host loss and the successor's recovery
unrun.store: the store column is conditional: #123 records no ST1 to ST8 qualification, and no store observation is a cited receipt

controller-reset.meaning: a controller reset after a quiesced close recovers warm on the same host and volume

unrun.model: no model projection runs a controller reset; the joins check the protocol, not the device
unrun.store: the store column is conditional: #123 records no ST1 to ST8 qualification, and no store observation is a cited receipt

process-kill.meaning: a killed owner process restarts warm on the same host and volume

unrun.model: no model projection runs a process kill; the joins check the protocol, not the process
unrun.store: the store column is conditional: #123 records no ST1 to ST8 qualification, and no store observation is a cited receipt

actual-volume-loss.meaning: actual volume loss provisions a replacement volume and starts cold; the cold control never stands for host loss

unrun.model: no model projection runs actual volume loss
unrun.store: the store column is conditional: #123 records no ST1 to ST8 qualification, and no store observation is a cited receipt

retention.set: the eligible set S at the certified recovery cut and frontier

reopen.claim: the fleet reopens after an operator store restore

excluded.host-failure: #30: a host-failure witness must survive on another host or failure domain
excluded.fis: the fis-read, fis-write and fis-stop profiles, judged by scripts/fis-controller.py
excluded.exclusion-and-successor: the catalog owners: the Exclusion and Successor sites stay undecided until they ratify them, and an unratified site earns no credit
excluded.staging: each separately owned staging package keeps its owner and its own judge

unrun.power-loss: backend durability and power loss are unmeasured: the reset and kill leave the host and volume powered, and no case cuts volume power
unrun.provider-phenomena: unresolved provider phenomena stay unmeasured: the END provider contract and holder-only runtime preemption are open, and the model cases resting on them are blocked
unrun.store-restore: no case restores the store, so the reopen claim has no run behind it
unrun.trace-replay: registered model-to-Rust trace replay of the history cases is open: hand-written tests witness their outcomes, and no trace binds a test to its model case
unrun.package-retention: the CR-1 and PK-1 retention verdict judges the served set, the unaffected bytes and the warm-load install; no package row measures fault-local damage or the recent unprotected suffix
unrun.package-conservation: the CR-1 and PK-1 residuals verdict and their proxy sample residuals once the second tenure's reservations drop, and no checkpoint or frontier publication follows, so neither cites conservation and the publish-aligned boundary is unmeasured for those classes

assumptions.model: a model result holds within its declared finite bounds under END, DURABLE and NEW-EXCLUSION, a model retention result also rests on the #148 lineage-fence premises, and neither is an inductive proof
assumptions.simulation: a seeded simulation run reports counts, work and ticks, never hardware latency, and a discovery run is no powered confirmation
assumptions.proxy: a simulated-device proxy carries no hardware credit
assumptions.hardware: a hardware cell credits only its own class and profile on a supported matching platform row
assumptions.store: a store-dependent result is conditional on the #123 store qualification
assumptions.sizing: a sizing scenario is conditional, its probability not identified, and carries no verdict
